_doc: What of BC this tree translates, and it is a WHITELIST. A namespace is in scope when the LONGEST matching prefix -- case-insensitive, on a dot boundary -- comes from `include`; an `exclude` entry wins over a shorter `include` prefix, which is what makes a carve-out possible. No match at all is out of scope. `Microsoft` is whitelisted WHOLE, because the goal is the complete BC business functionality and not a subset; what is carved out of it is the CLOUD GLUE -- Dataverse, D365 sync, Graph, PowerBI, Booking -- which has nothing to talk to in a standalone ERP. `System.*` is whitelisted per sub, because that is where the platform glue lives. THIS IS THE PREDECESSOR'S OWN SCOPE, entry for entry: `~/Git/openerp/scripts/transpiler/scope.json`, where the border cases were decided by the user and are recorded in its WI-990 -- CRM stays whole except Outlook, because Microsoft.CRM.Team is Salesperson (table 13) and Microsoft.CRM.Contact is 5050 and both are document foundation; e-invoicing stays whole INCLUDING its transport, because 'exclude the interfaces' meant cloud sync and not sending an e-document.
_area_doc: A file that declares NO namespace is decided by the top-level folder it sits in instead. W1's test suite is 91 % namespace-less, so the folder is the only signal it has. `CRM integration` is Dataverse sync and goes; the real CRM tests live under ERM and Marketing and stay. A `-Internal` suffix marks a test of the test framework.
